_about: Settings for this city's discovery places layer (engine/discover/build.py), docs/toronto/data/discover.geojson: places the City describes in its own open data, plus hand-checked viewpoints, for Along the way and the app. No businesses on the website (the user, November 17, 2026: they're for the iOS app). Keys: sources (each a dataset: id, url, credit, licence; name, text, link and word = its columns, word joined with ' · '; lat and lon columns, or a GeoJSON 'geometry' column; keep = {column: regex} rows must match; skip = regex on the name to leave out; kinds = rules in order, the first that matches gives the kind: {kind, match: regex, field: column, default the name}, a rule with no match catches the rest); words = the line under the name when a source has none; dedupe_m = metres within which two rows with the same name are one place (the first source wins, later ones fill in a missing text or link); viewpoints = the hand-kept file of viewpoints. Kinds: art (public artworks), history, park, library, view, and for the rows no earlier rule claims: faith (places of worship), rec (community centres, recreation, youth and community services), nature (greenbelts, trees, wetlands), arts (arts centres, studios, venues), then history (streets, addresses, plazas, Indigenous places: the City's text is about their past). The descriptions are the City's words, quoted with credit under the Open Government Licence - Toronto, never rewritten.
